To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cowpea is a suitable weaning food and its addition into maize-based weaning foods improves their nutritional and functional properties.
cowpea-f fortification of maize dough was effective in improving its nutritional value.

cowpeas can be successfully used as an ingredient in weaning foods, and that the fermentation of maize dough and cowpea addition can be used to improve the nutritional quality, and reduce the bulk density of maize dough.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a weaning food based on fermented maize dough, cowpea, sorghum malt and other locally available ingredients.
the development of a weaning food based on cowpea and maize.
the development of a weaning food based on cowpea, which is a major legume in the Ghanaian diet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study has provided useful information on the development of cowpea-based weaning food.

the cowpea-f fortification of maize dough was effective in terms of reducing the stachyose content, increasing protein content, lowering the bulk density and improving the functional properties of maize dough.
the cowpea-f fortification of fermented maize dough is a viable option in the production of weaning foods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cowpeas were successfully incorporated into maize flour to produce a weaning food with acceptable sensory properties.
the cowpeas are rich in protein, fat, ash, carbohydrates, minerals, vitamins and other nutrients.
the addition of germinated cereal malt to 3-day maize dough reduced the bulk density of the dough, but the effect was not significant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cowpea flour can be used to replace maize flour in the preparation of fermented maize dough-based weaning porridge.
the addition of cowpea to maize dough increases the protein content of the dough and the stachyose content of the dough is reduced.
the use of cowpea flour in weaning foods can be improved by germination and/or fermentation of the maize dough prior to fortification.
